title: The Pulse, Friday 23 October 2026
tldr: Anthropic donated Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation, joining MCP. The Decisions API from OpenAI cuts classification cost by skipping generation. NVIDIA's OpenShell is a sandboxed runtime for agent fleets, and formal verification is starting to work at scale.

models.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
models.summary: Agent Skills — the pattern Claude Code uses to give agents reusable procedures — joins MCP as an open standard under the Agentic AI Foundation.
models.why: Botterfly's skills live in this pattern; if it becomes the cross-platform standard, we can share our library with other agent runtimes.

models.title: Claude API now available through Google Cloud
models.summary: The full Claude API, including Managed Agents and Opus 5.5 fast mode, is now reachable through Google Cloud projects with IAM and Marketplace billing.
models.why: Clients already on Google Cloud can reach Claude without new vendor onboarding.

models.title: OpenAI Decisions API
models.summary: A new endpoint for fast, low-cost classification and routing: it evaluates inputs and returns structured decision labels without generating full responses.
models.why: Routing and filtering logic in agents and pipelines — like call grading or triage — can drop latency and cost by skipping the generation phase.

research.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
research.summary: Naive RAG (dense retrieval and reranking over raw conversation history) matches or beats complex agentic memory systems on long-context benchmarks.
research.why: Memory is a bottleneck for our voice agents and Botterfly; this suggests the simplest approach may be enough before we build a mutation layer.

research.title: Prompting Strategy Effects Depend on the Judge: A Multilingual Study of LLM-as-a-Judge Robustness
research.summary: Chain-of-Thought and role conditioning prompts improve some judge models but harm others, and effects vary across languages.
research.why: We use LLM-as-a-Judge for call grading and internal code review; this says prompt strategies must be tested per model and language, not copied.

research.title: IQuest-Q1: A 320B sparse MoE model for CLI agents
research.summary: A sparse Mixture-of-Experts foundation model with 320B total parameters (15B activated), trained for CLI agent tasks with a two-stage curriculum.
research.why: Large sparse models built for terminal agents are a pattern we might tap for self-hosted Botterfly alternatives.

research.title: FusionEval: Benchmarking Model Fusion for Large Language Models
research.summary: A benchmark for evaluating model fusion — merging expert models into one — with tasks covering reasoning, tool use, and long chains of thought.
research.why: Model fusion could let us combine a coding expert and a planning expert into one deployed model without full retraining.

releases.title: LangChain-core 1.7.0
releases.summary: Tool-call args now stream as `tool-call-delta` slices instead of `block-delta` snapshots. Pin `langchain-core<1.7` to keep snapshot behavior.
releases.why: Breaking change for anything reading raw stream events. Update before it catches us mid-sprint.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.68.0
releases.summary: New MCP tool for listing LLM connections, Topics treemap and grid views, and per-connection socket logging for the AI gateway.
releases.why: We use Langfuse for tracing; Topics view and connection logging help debug multi-model flows.

hackernews.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
hackernews.summary: Anthropic's research shows LLMs can now automate formal verification at scale: proving code properties that previously required manual theorem-prover expertise.
hackernews.why: Formal verification has been a research oddity; this makes it engineering-feasible. We could verify critical paths in call flows or agent harnesses.

hackernews.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents
hackernews.summary: NVIDIA released OpenShell, a sandboxed agent execution environment for running agent code with isolation, resource limits, and no internet.
hackernews.why: Agent sandboxing is still an open problem; this is a production take from NVIDIA. Worth comparing to Hermes's execution model.

hackernews.title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business
hackernews.summary: Indian CA eMudhra is exiting the SSL/TLS business after security concerns prompted OS and browser vendors to plan distrust. A full OTP bypass was published.
hackernews.why: Any service using eMudhra certificates needs to rotate before browsers drop trust. Check client deployments.

hackernews.title: Tell HN: I unknowingly broke the PHP RCE embargo. I am sorry.
hackernews.summary: A researcher accidentally published a PHP RCE exploit ahead of the coordinated disclosure, prompting mass exploitation before patches were widely applied.
hackernews.why: PHP RCE in production means patch now. Check every service running PHP.

hackernews.title: OpenAI CLI
hackernews.summary: OpenAI released an official CLI for completions, embeddings, and fine-tuning, with streaming output and JSON schema mode.
hackernews.why: A first-party CLI simplifies scripting OpenAI calls in pipelines and cron jobs. Worth knowing the shape if clients ask for it.

x_posts.title: Nous Research CEO on agents and digital sovereignty
x_posts.summary: Dillon Rolnick (Nous Research) and Matthew Prince (Cloudflare) discussed agents, the future of the internet, and digital sovereignty at a Union Square Ventures event.
x_posts.why: Cloudflare's view on agent infrastructure and digital sovereignty is a strategic signal for where the ecosystem is heading.

x_posts.title: Hermes + Cua Spaces: shared Linux/macOS/Windows environments
x_posts.summary: Hermes can now run in a Cua Space — a Linux, macOS, or Windows environment on hardware you own, where the team can watch live, step in, and hand control back.
x_posts.why: Collaborative agent supervision for complex tasks. Interesting for Botterfly working on long-running client projects.
